Thanks again for the warm onboarding sessions last month — Sparkwell is seeing steady usage and we really appreciate the SparkGrant credit pool the accelerator provided. Quick ask: we just crossed the expected free-credits runway sooner than planned because of an unanticipated spike in inference volume.

Our technical roadmap now requires predictable throughput for the next 6 months and we'd like to propose converting the remaining SparkGrant balance into a committed Dedicated discount (monthly reserved capacity) instead of the standard rollover. Specifically:
- Remaining credits: ~$12k equivalent (see attached statement).
- Proposed conversion: apply the $12k as a one-time credit toward a 6-month Dedicated commit with a 10% discount on standard Dedicated rates, with an option to renew month-to-month after 6 months.

I understand this is non-standard. Jordan at VC Bridge recommended I reach out to you directly to see if Redwood has a conversion path or promotional exception we can use.

Attached: credit_statement_Q1.pdf (statement of current SparkGrant usage/remaining).

If this is feasible, we can get legal to sign an amendment (happy to use your MAP template) and accelerate onboarding into Dedicated.

Best,

Thanks for the ping — quick operational note: we can convert program credits into billing credits against an invoice, but applying them as an evergreen percentage discount on Dedicated reservations is not standard and requires leadership sign-off (finance + revenue ops). That said, we've done one precedent earlier this year for a cohort partner (see internal ticket FIN-2028-112).

Process I recommend:
1) Confirm the exact USD value of credits and get the partner to sign the MAP amendment (they've already drafted signed-MAP-v1.docx).
2) We can apply the $12,000 as a one-time credit to the earliest invoice for the Reserved Dedicated commit (effectively reducing the pre-paid commitment by $12k). If they want the equivalent as an ongoing % discount, we need CFO approval and a minimum 12-month commit (we don't normally do 6-mo discounts).
3) Required approvals: Revenue Ops (me), Partnerships (Ben), and Rev Ops manager + Sales leadership for any deviation from the 12-month minimum.

Attached: FIN-2028-112-summary.pdf (precedent summary) — forwarding internal stub.

If Ben and Sergio are comfortable with the one-time-credit -> reserved-commit approach, I'll draft the billing addendum and coordinate the DocuSign link. If they insist on a recurring discount for 6 months, I need a write-up and manager approval before we proceed.

— Monica
